findings.title: Split review reports keep only the first part's usage
findings.description: In `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review_fold.py:81-87`, `_metadata()` starts from `dict(parts[0].metadata)` and only sums `TOOL_CALLS_MADE_KEY`; it never merges `USAGE_KEY` from later parts. `ReviewAction._run_part` stamps a separate usage record on each part in `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review.py:431-505`, but `_review()` returns `fold_review_parts(results)`, so the persisted `StepState.action_results` row has only part 1's tokens, turns, cost, and duration. `src/squadron/stats/reviews_report.py:55-86` excludes pipeline artifacts carrying `runId`, so those per-part artifacts are not counted by `sq stats reviews`; `src/squadron/stats/usage_report.py#run_usage_report` totals only the folded row. A two-part tasks review therefore under-reports spend for part 2. Aggregate all per-part `USAGE_KEY` records or persist all part records, and add a behavior test with two distinct usage records.

findings.title: Compact failures discard the LLM usage they already spent
findings.description: In `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/compact.py:74-88`, `capture` and `started` are created before the SDK compact call, but the `except Exception` branch returns a failed `ActionResult` with no `metadata` and no `stamp()`. `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:205-237` attaches `exc.telemetry` to `ProviderError`, and `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:456-497` can also raise during `_reconnect()` after the summary turn has already produced telemetry; in both cases the compact action loses the record. This violates slice 175 D5/D6 and success criteria 2 and 4: failed compact actions should carry `metadata.usage` and duration. Capture telemetry on both provider failures and post-capture reconnect failures, stamp the failed result, and add a regression test.

findings.title: Compact usage records omit alias, profile, and alias pricing
findings.description: The success path in `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/compact.py:90-98` calls `capture.record_from_telemetry(None, ...)`, so `UsageCapture._build` in `src/squadron/pipeline/usage_capture.py:180-207` sets `alias=None` and `profile=None`, and cannot apply `price_usage()` fallback when provider cost is absent. `src/squadron/cli/stats_views.py#cost_cell` depends on `record.alias` for the `api-rate equiv.` subscription label, and `src/squadron/models/aliases.py#price_usage` needs the alias to price non-SDK costs. Compact rows therefore lack profile/alias attribution and can show subscription provider cost as ordinary money. Resolve `summary_model` through `context.resolver.resolve_full(...)` or otherwise pass a `ResolvedModel`, and test a subscription alias plus an alias-only-pricing case.

findings.title: `sq stats reviews` scans non-review artifacts as review rows
findings.description: In `src/squadron/stats/reviews_report.py:55-86`, `reviews_usage_report()` globs every top-level `*.md` and filters only by `slice` and `runId`; it never validates `docType`. `src/squadron/review/resolution_artifact.py#render_resolution` writes `docType: review-resolution` into the same `REVIEWS_DIR`, and `src/squadron/documents/schema.py#RESOLUTION_DOC_TYPE` defines that non-review type. These files parse as mappings, have no `runId`, and are appended as `ReviewUsageRow`s with all usage fields `None`, producing extra rows in a report whose contract is one row per standalone review artifact. This is also an external file boundary, so Python rules call for schema validation rather than ad hoc key checks. Validate `docType == DocType.REVIEW` before `_row()` and add a regression test with a resolution artifact.

findings.title: Unreadable review artifacts crash the stats scan instead of being skipped
findings.description: At `src/squadron/stats/reviews_report.py:66-71`, `read_frontmatter(path)` is called without handling `OSError` or `UnicodeDecodeError`. `src/squadron/documents/frontmatter.py#read_frontmatter` calls `path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`, so a permission error, a file removed between `glob()` and read, or invalid UTF-8 escapes the report core; `src/squadron/cli/commands/stats.py:50-66` has no top-level guard. The failure table only covers `front is None` for malformed YAML or a missing block. Failure-Mode Enumeration requires each new I/O failure to be observable at WARNING+ and covered by a test; here one bad artifact aborts the whole report with a traceback. Catch read errors, log a WARNING naming the path, increment `skipped`, and test an unreadable or invalid-UTF-8 artifact.

findings.title: `stats reviews --json` is not JSON when the reviews directory is absent
findings.description: In `src/squadron/cli/commands/stats.py:58-64`, `report.missing_dir` is checked before `as_json`; the command prints `No review directory at ...` and returns. For `sq stats reviews --json` in a project without `project-documents/user/reviews/`, stdout is a human sentence, so `json.loads()` clients fail even though `--json` is documented for both subcommands. The missing-directory case should emit an empty JSON report, including `missing_dir`, empty rows, and empty totals, while preserving exit code 0. `tests/cli/test_stats.py:194-202` covers only the table form; add the `--json` case.

findings.title: Alias files are reread on hot capture and stats paths
findings.description: `src/squadron/models/aliases.py#get_all_aliases` calls `load_builtin_aliases()` and `load_user_aliases()`; both read TOML from disk, and there is no cache. `src/squadron/pipeline/usage_capture.py:180-207` calls `resolve_cost()` → `price_usage()` → `get_all_aliases()` for each non-SDK LLM action when provider cost is absent, adding synchronous file I/O to the async run path despite the design's "capture adds no I/O" bound and the Python rule that sync work inside `async def` must be bounded under 1 ms. `src/squadron/cli/stats_views.py#cost_cell` and `src/squadron/stats/reviews_report.py#_record` also call `get_all_aliases()` per row/artifact, so `sq stats` can perform repeated alias-file reads. Cache the alias table per process or pass a loaded alias mapping/settings object into these boundaries, and add a test that asserts no repeated alias file reads.

findings.title: Review cost resolution bypasses the run-level warning dedupe
findings.description: In `src/squadron/review/review_client.py:310-318`, `run_review_with_profile()` calls `resolve_cost(..., set())` on both success and `ProviderError` paths, while `src/squadron/pipeline/usage_capture.py:180-207` calls `resolve_cost()` with `UsageCapture._warned`. `src/squadron/models/aliases.py#price_usage` uses that set to emit one WARNING per alias. A pipeline with several reviews of a partially priced alias gets one WARNING per review from `review_client`, and `UsageCapture.record_from_error()` can recompute the same cost with a different dedupe set. This duplicates cost resolution and violates the design's single dedupe-set ownership. Pass the run's warned set into `run_review_with_profile()` or reuse `exc.cost_usd`/`exc.cost_basis` when stamping error records, and test repeated warnings.

findings.title: New tests do not cover the critical usage-report failure paths
findings.description: The tests added alongside implementation cover happy paths, but the new critical behaviors are not asserted. `tests/pipeline/actions/test_review_action_parts.py#TestFold` checks split-review outputs and summed tool calls but not `USAGE_KEY` aggregation; `tests/stats/test_reviews_report.py:6-18` writes only `docType: review`, so non-review artifacts and unreadable frontmatter are unexercised; `tests/cli/test_stats.py:194-202` checks missing-directory table output but not `stats reviews --json`; and the compact failure tests in the diff do not assert `metadata.usage`. These are behavior-level regressions that can silently under-report spend or break machine consumers. Add tests with the fixes, following the test-with pattern: split review with two usage records, compact failure/reconnect failure with telemetry, resolution artifact, unreadable artifact, and missing-dir `--json`.

structured_findings.summary: Split review reports keep only the first part's usage
